name: Question 15
problem:
A company collected data on the sale price (in thousands of dollars) of a particular used car model and the car's age (in years). This data is shown below.

| Age $(x)$ | **$4$** | **$5$** | **$6$** | **$7$** | **$8$** |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Price $(y)$ | $12$ | $10$ | $8.5$ | $7$ | $6.5$ |

Find the line of the form $y={\beta }_{0}+{\beta }_{1}x$ that best fits the data above. According to the model, what will be the sale price of a model that is $10$ years old, assuming the trend continues?

*Hint: You can use the fact that*

$$
({X}^{T}\,X)^{-1}=\frac{1}{10}[\begin{aligned}38 & -6 \\ -6 & 1\end{aligned}],\,{X}^{T}y=[\begin{aligned}44 \\ 250\end{aligned}],
$$

*where $X$ is the corresponding design matrix and $y$ is the observation vector.*
worked_solution:
The coefficients of the line that best fits the data can be found as the least-squares solution $\overset{^}{\beta }$ to the system 

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{X}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}1 & 4 \\ 1 & 5 \\ 1 & 6 \\ 1 & 7 \\ 1 & 8\end{aligned}]}}\overset{\beta }{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}{\beta }_{0} \\ {\beta }_{1}\end{aligned}]}} & =\overset{y}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}12 \\ 10 \\ 8.5 \\ 7 \\ 6.5\end{aligned}]}},\end{aligned}
$$

where $X$ is the design matrix, $\beta $ is the parameter vector, and $y$ is the observation vector.

Pre-multiplying this equation by ${X}^{T},$ we obtain the corresponding normal equation

$$
{X}^{T}\,X\overset{^}{\beta }={X}^{T}y.
$$

Since the columns of $X$ are linearly independent, the matrix ${X}^{T}X$ is invertible and 

$$
\overset{^}{\beta }=({X}^{T}\,X)^{-1}{X}^{T}y.
$$

Substituting the given values of $({X}^{T}X)^{-1}$ and ${X}^{T}y$ into the formula, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{^}{\beta } & =({X}^{T}\,X)^{-1}{X}^{T}\,y \\  & =\frac{1}{10}[\begin{aligned}38 & -6 \\ -6 & 1\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}44 \\ 250\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}17.2 \\ -1.4\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have the line $y=17.2-1.4x.$

Finally, to predict the selling price of a car of the same model that is $10$ years old, we substitute $x=10$ into the equation of the line:

$$
\begin{aligned}y & =17.2-1.4(10) \\  & =3.2\end{aligned}
$$

So, according to the model, the sale price will be $$3\,200.$

**Note**: Since we're extrapolating ($x=10$ is not within the range of the original set of $x$-values), our result *may* be unreliable.

Question 15
?

A company collected data on the sale price (in thousands of dollars) of a particular used car model and the car's age (in years). This data is shown below.

Age (x) 4 5 6 7 8
Price (y) 12 10 8.5 7 6.5

Find the line of the form y=β0+β1x that best fits the data above. According to the model, what will be the sale price of a model that is 10 years old, assuming the trend continues?

Hint: You can use the fact that (XTX)−1=110[38−6−61],XTy=[44250], where X is the corresponding design matrix and y is the observation vector.

a
$2800
b
$4400
c
$4200
d
$3200
e
$3700
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

The coefficients of the line that best fits the data can be found as the least-squares solution β^ to the system

[1415161718]⏞X[β0β1]⏞β=[12108.576.5]⏞y,

where X is the design matrix, β is the parameter vector, and y is the observation vector.

Pre-multiplying this equation by XT, we obtain the corresponding normal equation

XTXβ^=XTy.

Since the columns of X are linearly independent, the matrix XTX is invertible and

β^=(XTX)−1XTy.

Substituting the given values of (XTX)−1 and XTy into the formula, we get

β^=(XTX)−1XTy=110[38−6−61]⋅[44250]=[17.2−1.4].

Therefore, we have the line y=17.2−1.4x.

Finally, to predict the selling price of a car of the same model that is 10 years old, we substitute x=10 into the equation of the line:

y=17.2−1.4(10)=3.2

So, according to the model, the sale price will be $3200.

Note: Since we're extrapolating (x=10 is not within the range of the original set of x-values), our result may be unreliable.
